projects.title: MedTriage Rural AI — Multimodal Clinical Triage Copilot
projects.tagline: Reducing rural primary-care diagnostic delays with offline-capable multimodal AI triage.

step1_competition.name: Gemini API Developer Competition
step1_competition.theme: AI for Social Impact & Accessible Healthcare
step1_competition.description: Build high-impact applications using multimodal generative AI to solve urgent community challenges in healthcare, education, or sustainability.
step1_competition.targetTechnology: Google Gemini Multimodal API, Next.js, Edge Offline Cache, PostgreSQL
step1_competition.additionalContext: Focus on underserved rural clinics (Puskesmas) in Indonesia where specialist physicians are scarce.

analysis.themeBreakdown: The theme demands more than a generic medical Q&A wrapper. Judges prioritize measurable patient/clinician workflow improvements, safe clinical decision support (non-diagnostic triage escalation), and resilient operation in low-resource settings.

relevantIndustries.name: Rural Primary Healthcare (Puskesmas)
relevantIndustries.relevanceWhy: Frontline triage nurses handle high patient volumes with limited specialist consultation access.

relevantIndustries.name: Telemedicine & Referral Triage
relevantIndustries.relevanceWhy: Structured pre-referral summaries drastically cut emergency hospital intake delays.

mainChallenges: Hallucination risk in clinical settings requiring strict protocol grounding.
Intermittent internet connectivity in remote archipelago clinics.
High cognitive load for frontline nurses documenting patient intake.

technologyOpportunities.opportunityWhy: Simultaneously processes nurse voice notes, vital sign chart photos, and WHO/MoH clinical guidelines.
Pins every triage recommendation to official Ministry of Health (Kemenkes) standard operating procedures.

potentialProblemAreas.relevanceWhy: Late identification of high-risk maternal and infectious cases causes preventable mortality.
Nurses spend 15–25 minutes per complex case writing referral letters manually.

judgeFocusAreas: Depth and necessity of Gemini multimodal capabilities (voice + image + long-context protocols).
Empirical validation of the healthcare bottleneck with verifiable public health statistics.
Safety guardrails: human-in-the-loop verification and citation transparency.

recommendedInnovationDirections.title: Protocol-Grounded Multimodal Triage Copilot
recommendedInnovationDirections.description: Combine voice intake, photo capture of paper vitals, and official clinical guidelines into a 60-second red-flag triage scorer.
recommendedInnovationDirections.whyRelevant: Directly showcases multimodal AI strength while solving a documented clinical bottleneck.

recommendedInnovationDirections.title: Automated SBAR Referral Packet Generator
recommendedInnovationDirections.description: Instantly structure patient findings into standardized Situation-Background-Assessment-Recommendation (SBAR) hospital handoffs.
recommendedInnovationDirections.whyRelevant: Produces immediate, measurable time savings that can be demonstrated live to judges in under 2 minutes.

step2_judgeCriteria.overallInterpretation: With 60% of the score concentrated in Innovation (30%) and Impact (30%), the winning strategy must combine verifiable public-health evidence with a visibly multimodal live product demo.
strategicPriorities: Lead with verified clinical triage delay evidence (Impact: 30%).
Demonstrate simultaneous voice + clinical chart image analysis (Innovation: 30%).
Enforce human-in-the-loop nurse sign-off and protocol citations (Feasibility & Technical: 30%).

step3_problemDiscovery.whoExperiences: Frontline triage nurses and general practitioners at rural primary healthcare clinics (Puskesmas) in underserved regions.
step3_problemDiscovery.biggestDifficulty: Rapidly cross-referencing complex symptoms, vital signs, and national clinical guidelines during peak clinic hours while manually writing hospital referral summaries.
step3_problemDiscovery.frequency: Daily — occurring across 30 to 60 patient intakes per clinic every morning.
step3_problemDiscovery.impact: 15–25 minutes spent per complex referral case on manual documentation, contributing to delayed emergency escalations and clinician burnout.
step3_problemDiscovery.currentWorkarounds: Static PDF guideline booklets, WhatsApp messages to on-call doctors, and handwritten paper referral forms.
step3_problemDiscovery.whyInsufficient: Static PDFs take too long to search during urgent intake, and unstructured WhatsApp messages omit critical clinical red flags.

analysis.targetUser: Frontline Triage Nurses & Rural Primary Care Clinicians (Puskesmas)

userPersona.name: Ners Rina Wulandari, S.Kep
userPersona.role: Senior Triage Nurse at a Rural Community Health Center
userPersona.demographics: 29 years old, handles 45+ patients/day with 1 general practitioner on duty
goals: Identify high-risk emergency cases within 2 minutes of arrival
Generate accurate SBAR hospital referral letters without delaying the queue
frustrations: Searching 200-page PDF clinical guidelines mid-consultation is impractical
Re-typing handwritten vital signs into referral forms wastes critical time
userPersona.quote: When ten patients arrive at once, I need immediate protocol verification and a ready-to-send referral summary—not another complex form.

painPoints: High cognitive load matching multi-symptom presentations against national clinical guidelines.
Time-consuming manual transcription of paper vital logs into digital referral letters.
Inconsistent handoff quality when referring high-risk patients to regional hospitals.

currentAlternatives.name: Printed / PDF Clinical SOP Manuals
currentAlternatives.limitation: Passive reference; cannot actively flag risk combinations from patient vitals.

currentAlternatives.name: Unstructured WhatsApp Consultations
currentAlternatives.limitation: Lacks standardized SBAR structure, audit trail, and clinical guideline citations.

analysis.problemFrequency: Daily (30–60 patient encounters per clinic per day)
analysis.problemStatement: Frontline triage nurses at rural primary care clinics experience delays and documentation overload when assessing complex patient presentations because clinical guidelines are trapped in static manuals and referral summaries are drafted manually, resulting in 15–25 minute administrative bottlenecks per referral and delayed escalation of high-risk cases.
rootCauseAnalysis: Disconnect between point-of-care patient intake (voice + paper vitals) and static clinical guideline documents.
Lack of automated SBAR clinical summarization tailored to primary-to-secondary care referrals.
Shortage of specialist physicians at frontline clinics to provide immediate second opinions.
analysis.validationDisclaimer: Note: This problem statement is structured from user workflow analysis and desk research. Direct field usability testing with clinic nurses is scheduled as part of the validation roadmap.

step4_evidenceValidation.searchQuery: clinical decision support triage primary care rural healthcare referral delay

evidenceItems.finding: World Health Organization (WHO) reports that primary health care workforce shortages and administrative burden significantly impact timely care delivery in low- and middle-income regions.
evidenceItems.supportingStatistic: Global shortfall of 10 million health workers projected by 2030, disproportionately affecting rural primary care facilities.
evidenceItems.sourceTitle: Health workforce overview and primary care capacity
evidenceItems.relevanceToProblem: Validates the structural clinician shortage in rural clinics that forces triage nurses to manage high patient volumes.
evidenceItems.businessOrSocialOpportunity: Decision-support tools that save 10+ minutes per complex intake multiply effective clinician capacity.
evidenceItems.verificationNote: Official WHO public health authority resource.

evidenceItems.finding: Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) integrated into primary care triage improve adherence to clinical guidelines and reduce diagnostic escalation delays.
evidenceItems.supportingStatistic: Systematic reviews in NPJ Digital Medicine and BMJ show structured CDSS improves guideline adherence by 12%–28% in primary care triage.
evidenceItems.sourceTitle: Computerised clinical decision support systems for primary care (Crossref / BMJ)
evidenceItems.relevanceToProblem: Demonstrates peer-reviewed empirical evidence that protocol-grounded triage software measurably improves frontline care.
evidenceItems.businessOrSocialOpportunity: High institutional adoption potential across public health networks seeking standardized referral quality.
evidenceItems.verificationNote: Verified DOI via Crossref academic registry.

evidenceItems.finding: Standardized SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) communication protocols significantly reduce clinical handoff errors during patient referrals.
evidenceItems.supportingStatistic: Implementation of structured SBAR handoffs reduces critical omission errors during emergency transfers by over 30%.
evidenceItems.sourceTitle: Impact of SBAR communication protocol on patient safety in clinical handovers
evidenceItems.sourceOrganization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (PubMed Central)
evidenceItems.relevanceToProblem: Supports automating SBAR referral packets as a high-impact, clinically validated intervention.
evidenceItems.businessOrSocialOpportunity: Directly addresses hospital intake rejection and referral delays.

report.problemOverview: Rural primary healthcare facilities face severe clinician-to-patient ratio constraints while relying on manual paper vitals and static PDF guidelines for urgent triage.
report.supportingEvidenceSummary: Authoritative data from the World Health Organization (WHO) and peer-reviewed clinical informatics literature confirm both the structural workforce bottleneck and the efficacy of structured Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) and SBAR handoff automation.
statisticalInsights: 10M projected global health workforce deficit by 2030 (WHO), concentrated in rural primary care.
12%–28% improvement in clinical guideline adherence when frontline staff use structured CDSS.
>30% reduction in critical handoff omissions when using standardized SBAR referral templates.
report.researchFindingsSummary: Desk research confirms that passive digital manuals fail under time pressure; effective interventions must integrate directly into the intake workflow and produce actionable handoff artifacts.
report.marketOrSocialImpact: Deploying rapid multimodal triage across community health clinics can save thousands of nursing hours monthly and accelerate emergency maternal and infectious disease referrals.
evidenceGaps: Desk research is strong, but localized time-motion measurements inside target Puskesmas clinics should be collected during pilot testing.
report.opportunityAnalysis: By combining multimodal capture (voice + photo of vital charts) with strict guideline grounding, the project bridges the gap between clinical compliance and speed.
report.deskVsCustomerDistinction: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: The citations above represent verified desk research from academic and public health authorities, not direct primary user interviews. Field validation with practicing triage nurses is required to validate UI ergonomics.

step5_solutionGenerator.comparisonSummary: While Option 2 (Patient Self-Triage Kiosk) and Option 3 (Hospital Referral Portal) address parts of the problem, Option 1 (MedTriage Rural AI — Multimodal Nurse Copilot) directly empowers the trained triage nurse, minimizes clinical safety risks via human-in-the-loop sign-off, and maximizes Gemini multimodal capabilities.
step5_solutionGenerator.recommendationReasoning: Recommended as the strongest competition entry because it aligns 100% with the 60% Innovation + Impact weight, avoids the regulatory hazard of autonomous patient self-diagnosis, and delivers a dramatic 60-second live demo.

alternatives.name: MedTriage Rural AI — Multimodal Nurse Triage Copilot
alternatives.conceptDescription: An AI-assisted clinical triage workspace where nurses capture a photo of paper vital logs and speak patient symptoms; the system cross-checks official clinical guidelines, flags red-flag urgency levels, and generates a one-click SBAR referral PDF.
alternatives.targetUser: Frontline Triage Nurses at Rural Primary Care Clinics
coreFunctionality: Multimodal Vital & Symptom Intake (Voice + Chart Photo OCR)
Protocol-Grounded Red-Flag Risk Stratification (Emergency / Urgent / Non-Urgent)
One-Click SBAR Hospital Referral Packet Generator with Guideline Citations
alternatives.innovation: Fuses simultaneous voice narration, handwritten vital chart extraction, and strict clinical SOP citation grounding in a single 60-second workflow.
alternatives.expectedImpact: Cuts complex triage & referral documentation time from 20 minutes to under 90 seconds while surfacing critical clinical red flags.
alternatives.feasibility: High — buildable within hackathon timeline using Gemini Multimodal JSON mode + Next.js.
alternatives.competitiveDifferentiation: Unlike generic medical chatbots, every output is strictly pinned to official clinical SOP passages and outputs a hospital-ready SBAR referral document.
alternatives.judgeAlignment: Directly showcases multimodal AI (Innovation 30%) on a WHO-validated problem (Impact 30%) with human-in-the-loop safety (Feasibility 15%).

alternatives.name: Direct-to-Patient WhatsApp Symptom Triage Bot
alternatives.conceptDescription: A conversational WhatsApp bot allowing rural citizens to self-report symptoms before visiting the clinic.
alternatives.innovation: Accessible voice-note interface over low-bandwidth messaging.
alternatives.expectedImpact: Reduces unnecessary clinic visits for mild conditions.
alternatives.feasibility: Moderate — requires WhatsApp Business API approval and carries higher clinical liability risk.
alternatives.judgeAlignment: High social reach, but judges often penalize direct-to-patient medical advice due to safety and hallucination liability.

alternatives.name: Regional Hospital Bed & Referral Matching Network
alternatives.conceptDescription: A real-time dashboard matching rural clinics with available ICU/specialist beds across regional hospitals.
alternatives.innovation: Predictive capacity routing across regional hospital networks.
alternatives.expectedImpact: Prevents referred patients from being turned away at full hospitals.
alternatives.feasibility: Low for a hackathon — depends heavily on multi-hospital EHR integration.
alternatives.judgeAlignment: Lighter use of generative AI; judges in an AI hackathon may view this primarily as a CRUD logistics app.

valueProposition.competitiveDifferentiation: Built specifically for nurse-in-the-loop triage compliance rather than unverified consumer symptom chatting.

techStackTable.rationale: Fast SSR/CSR hybrid rendering with built-in PWA capabilities for low-connectivity clinics.
Unified full-stack type safety and zero-overhead deployment within hackathon timelines.
ACID compliance for clinical audit logs plus vector search support for SOP retrieval.
Native multimodal ingestion (audio + image + text) with low latency and strict JSON schema outputs.
Deterministic, print-accurate SBAR and architecture document generation.

deliverables.systemOverview: MedTriage Rural AI uses a 3-tier architecture combining a responsive multimodal capture client, a stateless API orchestration layer with RAG guideline retrieval, and an audited PostgreSQL persistence store.
deliverables.architectureExplanation: When a nurse uploads a vital sign photo and voice recording, the backend validates the session, retrieves relevant clinical guideline passages from PostgreSQL, and invokes the Gemini Multimodal endpoint with a strict JSON schema contract.

componentResponsibilities.responsibility: Captures camera frames and WebAudio streams, compresses payloads, and renders structured triage cards.
Injects verified SOP protocol sections and enforces non-diagnostic decision-support guardrails.
Formats verified triage data into standardized A4 hospital referral documents.

deliverables.databaseDesign: Relational tables for Clinicians, TriageEncounters, VitalReadings, GuidelineCitations, and AuditLogs.
deliverables.apiIntegrationPlan: RESTful JSON endpoints (`POST /api/triage/analyze`, `POST /api/triage/signoff`, `GET /api/protocols/search`) with rate limiting.
deliverables.aiIntegrationStrategy: Use structured JSON schema enforcement so the LLM always returns `urgencyLevel`, `extractedVitals`, `redFlags[]`, `sopCitations[]`, and `sbarDraft`.
deliverables.securityConsiderations: PII scrubbing before external LLM calls, HTTPS/TLS encryption in transit, clinician session authentication, and mandatory human sign-off.
deliverables.deploymentStrategy: Continuous deployment via GitHub to Vercel with managed PostgreSQL and environment-isolated API keys.

technicalRisks.mitigation: Restrict AI reasoning strictly to retrieved SOP chunks and display verbatim source excerpts next to every alert.

technicalRisks.risk: Poor Lighting on Handwritten Vital Charts
technicalRisks.mitigation: Render extracted vitals in editable numeric inputs with confidence highlights for nurse verification.
